title: Context Check
user: Dyslexic software engineers and their reviewers who need to catch visually plausible identifier, config-key, and shell-command mistakes before they become production incidents.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An Ask HN participant describes a diligent colleague with a high typo rate causing late catches and production outages; linting and normal review have not solved it.
A product accessibility audit explicitly requests a dyslexia-friendly toggle to reduce reading friction.

recurrence: Two independent 2026 accounts connect dyslexia-related reading friction to work quality; the HN report calls out repeated late defects, making severity higher than ordinary spelling errors.
current_workaround: Rely on spell check, linters, code review, extra tests, or a colleague; these either miss domain tokens or add social friction.
incumbents_and_gap: LanguageTool, cspell, IDE linting, and Grammarly flag spelling, while font toggles only change presentation. They do not compare a change against repository vocabulary and flag confusable, near-duplicate tokens in context.
smallest_useful_product: Local VS Code extension that highlights newly introduced near-matches to existing identifiers, config keys, filenames, and commands; presents a one-line spoken/readable comparison and an explicit dismiss action. Non-goals: AI code generation, performance scoring, or diagnosis.
success_measure: At least 50% of pilot users retain the extension after four weeks and each reports one prevented wrong-key, wrong-file, or wrong-command change.
monetization: free — local-first adoption and accessibility trust matter more than billing; paid team policy/reporting can be evaluated later.
constraints: Never upload source by default; support disabling sensitive paths; suggestions must be explainable and avoid labeling a person or condition.
why_distinct: The unit of help is an explainable repository-context confusion, not generic grammar correction or a dyslexia-font clone.
